evidence: src/business/logic/BoxOffice.ts: constructor injects store abstractions `private readonly events: EventStore, private readonly tickets: TicketStore` and builds domain entities `new Event(...)` and `new Ticket(...)`

src/business/logic/GateLog.ts: constructor injects the raw ORM `private readonly prisma: PrismaService` and calls `prisma.scan.create({ data: { id: `${gate}:${code}`, code, gate, at: new Date() } })` and `this.prisma.scan.findMany()` directly, with no store or domain type

src/business/logic/BoxOffice.ts admit(): `ticket.admit(new Date()); await this.tickets.markScanned(...)` records a scan, while GateLog.scanned(code, gate) records a second scan without checking or linking to the ticket
src/business/logic/BoxOffice.ts: the row-to-Event mapping `new Event(d.id, d.title, d.venueCapacity, d.seatsSold, d.startsAt, d.priceCents)` is repeated in purchase() and listing()
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Both files cover ticketing and admission, but they don't use the module's abstractions the same way. BoxOffice.ts goes through dedicated persistence stores (EventStore, TicketStore). It turns their rows into domain entities (Event, Ticket) and puts its rules in those entities, raising domain errors when they are broken. GateLog.ts skips that pattern. It takes the raw PrismaService and calls prisma.scan.create and prisma.scan.findMany directly. It builds a scan id by hand (`${gate}:${code}`) and uses no domain type for a scan.

The scan concept is also split. BoxOffice.admit records a scan through ticket.admit and tickets.markScanned. GateLog.scanned records a scan in a separate table and doesn't check that the ticket exists or was admitted. So the 'ticket scanned' fact is written in two places, and nothing keeps the two records consistent.

A smaller issue: BoxOffice.ts builds an Event from a store row with the same line in two places, purchase and listing. That mapping should live in one place.

Import direction is out of scope and isn't counted here.

violations.message: Skips the module's store and entity pattern. It injects PrismaService and calls prisma.scan.create and findMany directly, with no store abstraction or domain Scan type, while BoxOffice uses EventStore, TicketStore and the Event and Ticket entities.

Splits the scan concept. GateLog.scanned writes its own scan record and doesn't check the ticket, while BoxOffice.admit records the scan through Ticket.admit and TicketStore.markScanned. The 'ticket scanned' fact lives in two places that nothing keeps consistent.
Repeats the row-to-Event mapping (`new Event(id, title, venueCapacity, seatsSold, startsAt, priceCents)`) in both purchase() and listing() instead of keeping it in one place.
